newsitem.title: GREECE: Family of missing English boy in Greek search.
newsitem.headline: Family of missing English boy in Greek search.

text.p: The grandparents of Briton Ben Needham, who disappeared five years ago from a Greek island at the age of two, said on Sunday that a nationwide television search rekindled their hopes for his recovery.
The private Star channel put on a three-hour show on Friday to find the English boy and hundreds of people, mainly from northern Greece, called in saying they had spotted Ben, now seven years old.

"After hundreds and hundreds of calls that we received during the show we feel that one of these is going to find Ben," the boy's grandmother, Christine Needham, told Reuters Television. "There is somebody who knows in this country and it just takes one person to speak. We feel very much closer."
The show's host, Costas Hardavellas, put up a computer picture of Ben at the age of seven and said all evidence collected in the programme would be given to police for further investigation.
Ben's grandparents, who flew in from England to take part in the programme, often burst into tears when somebody called in with a supposed recent spotting.

Hardavellas said the search was focused on the northern town of Volos. Ben disappeared in July 1991 while playing a few metres from a house his grandparents were renovating on the Aegean island of Kos.

A number of people have said they have spotted him around Greece but all sightings proved false alarms. Eddie Needham, the boy's grandfather, said a private benefactor in England had increased a 20,000 pound ($32,810) reward for Ben's recovery to half a million pounds.
Christine said her daughter and Ben's mother Karry Ann, were deeply troubled and bitter.

"She is deeply troubled. It has affected her mind although she pretends sometimes there is nothing wrong. Even if we find Ben she will never get totally well. She is angry and very bitter that this happened to her," she said. ($1=.6096 Pound)
